newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA OFFERS 76 FIRMS FOR SALE.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA OFFERS 76 FIRMS FOR SALE.

text.p: Bulgaria, currently in the throes of an economic crisis, plans to sell 76 firms as revenue from sell-offs is seen a major cash source for the debt-ridden state, a Privatisation Agency official said on Tuesday.

The list of firms earmarked for sell-offs, made available to Reuters, includes the country's chemical giants Sodi Devnya and Chimko Vratsa, Pirdop Copper Smelter, the aluminium producer Alumina and three cement plants among others.
Earlier this year the government announced a 25 percent sale of the Bulgarian Telecommunication Company (BTC).

A tender for consultancy assistance to the Posts and Communications Committee, the BTC and the government will be called by the end of October, Privatisation Agency executive director Veselin Blagoev told a news conference.
On Monday Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said the government relied on privatisation deals worth more than one billion dollars by the year-end to cover citizens' deposits in ailing banks.
The central bank put under special supervision nine ailing banks on Monday in a bid to stabilise the country's crumbling banking sector.
The Privatisation Agency list includes also textile and clothing firms, producers of machine tools, hardware, food, baverages, tobacco and glass and for paper and wood products.

Among tourist complexes is the Albena Black Sea resort with 39 hotels, hotel complex Slanchev Den at the St. Konstantin and Elena resort near the Black Sea port of Varna and hotels in Sofia such as Rodina, Grand Hotel Sofia, Novotel Evropa and Park Hotel Moskva.
Bulgaria received 77.2 billion levs from 1,329 privatisation deals sealed since the beginning of this year, Blagoev said.
Under the contracts the new owners also pledged to pay some 41 billion levs of companies' debts and invest 8.2 billion levs this year alone, he said.

Major deals included the sale of the Sheraton Sofia Hotel Balkan to South Korea's giant Daewoo Corp for $22.3 million and the electric tool maker Eltos to the German-registered Sparky Trading GmbH for 11.5 million German marks.
A 75 percent stake in the contry's second biggest oil refinery Plama, intitially slated for liquidation, was sold to Bulgaria's Euroenergy holding for 62 million levs.
Blagoev is leaving for the United States on Wednesday and will aslo visit Sweden and Finland at the beginning of October in an attempt to attract interest in Bulgaria's sell-offs.
